text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government chose Independent Trade Union leader Valer Xheka to resurrect an agreement on wages.
- An anti-Mafia delegation from Italy visited Albania to discuss the possible involvement of local rings with trafficking of drugs, arms and people.

- Students in the southern town of Gjirokaster threatened to boycott lessons next year if Albanian authorities did not move quickly to improve their conditions and accommodation. A power blackout has troubled students in Tirana.
- The right-wing Democratic Alliance Party decided to hold its first convention in March 29 next year.
- Ibrahim Rugova, self-declared leader of the ethnic Albanians in the Serbian province of Kosovo, was awarded the Honoris Causa at Saint Denis University in Paris.
- In an interview with daily Vehbi Alimuca, the president of Vefa Holding company told almost half a million depositors not to worry about money deposited in his pyramid scheme.
- The government and the Independent Trade Union agreed on inflation indexing, gradual wage increases and guaranteeing a real minimal salary in the private sector.
- One of the first pyramid schemes companies, Sudja, has guaranteed despositors they will get back their money starting Wednesday but with no returns.
- Some 700 senior officials have declared their properties and income to a verifying parliamentary commission.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will make a short visit to Albania on Wednesday and meet President Sali Berisha.
- Ilir Meta, a leader of the opposition Socialists, says his party should hold an extraordinary congress to solve the present crisis.
- The newspaper editorial hails protests by Serbian students in Belgrade and expresses the conviction they will be successful.
- The Islamic Conference passed a resolution on the situation in Kosovo, the Serbian province with an Albanian ethnic majority population.
